author: Susan Harrison
text:
Over the last couple of months we have noticed that the blood sugar monitor mounted on my diabetic husband's arm wasn't sending an alarm to his smart phone to alert us to the fact his blood sugar was occasionally either too high or too low. Both of these can be VERY DANGEROUS.
 
 After changing the arm monitor a few times but the problem persisting we got in touch with the company that makes them. After talking though pressing lots of buttons on the phone we were assured it was sorted. 
 
 The next week we had a day when his blood sugar on awakening was ridiculously high but NO ALARM. Later the same day it turned out he had injected too much insulin to bring it under control and had done too much physically carrying stuff about. His blood sugar dropped until it went too low and he was starting to go hypoglycemic and was in danger of passing out. This is VERY DANGEROUS. 

ONCE AGAIN THERE WAS NO ALARM.

A rapid phone call to the NHS diabetic nurse and then the company led to lots more button pressing on the smart phone before the company stated that it "WAS NO LONGER COMPATIBLE". Strange because previously it worked perfectly.

 What the actual??!? They've 'improved it' so much it no longer works and doesn't do its main job anymore. We thought we'd better publicise this in case other people are having similar problems.https://www.facebook.com/share/p/163Cpnz1zu/
